newsitem.title: ISRAEL: S&P, Moody's reaffirm Israel's credit rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P, Moody's reaffirm Israel's credit rating.

text.p: Standard & Poor's and Moody's have reaffirmed Israel's sovereign credit rating of A minus and A3 respectively, the Finance Ministry said on Sunday.
The ministry said in a statement that the credit rating agencies informed the ministry of their decision on Friday.
S&P's A minus is equivalent to Moody's A3.

The reaffirmation was made in advance of the implementation of Israel's programme to begin raising funds in the Eurobond market. On Tuesday, Israel will sign a framework accord with the seven international investment banks that will manage Israel's offerings.
Israel plans to raise $750 million over three years, including $200 million later this year.
The reaffirmation "shows the continued confidence and esteem they (the agencies) have for the Israeli economy," the ministry's statement said.

Last week the Finance Ministry and the Bank of Israel denied a local news report that Moody's had issued a warning of a possible lowering of Israel's credit rating. Moody's would not comment except to say Israel was not on watch.
